test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How many distinct temples are there in the Dilwara Temples complex?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dilwara Temples** are a world-famous group of **Svetambara Jain temples** located about 2.5 kilometers from the **Mount Abu** hill station, the only hill station in **Rajasthan**.
 
• There are **5** distinct temples in the complex, each dedicated to a different **Jain Tirthankara** and possessing its own unique architectural identity.
 
• These temples were built between the **11th and 16th centuries** (specifically between **1031 AD and 1582 AD**) during the reign of the **Chaulukya dynasty** (Solanki rulers).
 
• The complex is globally renowned for its extraordinary **architecture** and stunning **marble stone carvings**, often considered superior to the Taj Mahal in terms of intricate detailing.
 
• The five temples included in the complex are **Vimal Vasahi**, **Luna Vasahi**, **Pittalhar**, **Parshvanath**, and **Mahavir Swami**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vimal Vasahi Temple:**

 
 
• Built in **1031 AD** by **Vimal Shah**, a minister of the **Solanki King Bhimdev I**.
 
• It is dedicated to the **first Jain Tirthankara**, **Lord Rishabha** (also known as Adinath).
 
• The temple is famous for its "**Rang Mandap**," a central hall supported by **12 decorated pillars** and a magnificent carved dome.
 
 
 
• **Luna Vasahi Temple:**
 
 
• Constructed in **1230 AD** by two brothers, **Vastupal and Tejpal**, who were ministers of **Raja Vir Dhawal** of Gujarat.
 
• It is dedicated to the **22nd Tirthankara**, **Lord Neminatha**.
 
• The temple is noted for its "**Hathishala**" (elephant cell), featuring **10 marble elephants**, and its incredibly delicate pendant carvings in the central dome.
 
 
 
• **Pittalhar Temple:**
 
 
• This temple was built by **Bhima Shah**, another minister from Gujarat, during the **14th-15th century**.
 
• It is dedicated to **Lord Adinath** and houses a massive statue of the deity cast in **five metals** (Panchaloha), with **brass (Pittal)** being the dominant metal, giving the temple its name.
 
 
 
• **Parshvanath Temple (Khartar Vasahi):**
 
 
• Built between **1458 and 1459** by the **Mandlika** family, it is the tallest shrine in the Dilwara complex.
 
• It is dedicated to the **23rd Tirthankara**, **Lord Parshvanath**, and consists of a **three-story** building with grey stone carvings on the exterior walls.
 
 
 
• **Mahavir Swami Temple:**
 
 
• Completed in **1582**, it is the smallest and newest temple in the complex, dedicated to the **24th and last Tirthankara**, **Lord Mahavira**.
 
• Despite its small size, it features beautiful **wall paintings** on the upper walls of the porch, dating back to **1764**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Architectural Style:** The temples are built in the **Maru-Gurjara** style of architecture, which originated in **Western India**. This style is characterized by **ornate carvings**, **multiple shrines**, and **vaulted ceilings**.
 
• **Material Sourcing:** The **white marble** used for the construction was transported from the **Arasuri hills** near **Ambaji** in Gujarat, which was a massive logistical feat at the time.
 
• **Location:** Situated at a high altitude in the **Aravalli Range**, the site provides a serene environment conducive to **meditation** and religious activities.
 
• **Preservation:** The complex is managed by the **Seth Kalyanji Paramanandji Pedhi** trust and remains a vital **pilgrimage site** for the Jain community worldwide.
